procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, home, sister beside her. Still on capecitabine cycles; tired the second week of each cycle, recovers in the off week. Pain controlled on the palliative regimen. No confusion, vomiting or constipation lately. Home BP around 130/80.
Appears thin but bright on video.
Plan: continue. In-person visit with labs in April.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order renewal for lisinopril 20 and atorvastatin 20. Last BMP September, creatinine acceptable. Renewed 90 days x 3. Polyethylene glycol is over the counter.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: oncology and palliative care continuing; capecitabine ongoing, denosumab monthly. Pain steady. Energy low but gets out for short walks with her cane.
Meds per our list, reconciled verbally; no changes she is aware of.
Exam: thin, slight further weight loss. Alert. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Diffuse bony tenderness over the low back. No edema.
A/P: labs for calcium, kidneys, counts and lipids. BP fine on lisinopril. Summer video visit, then wellness/flu in the fall.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calcium normal on the denosumab. Hemoglobin still a little low, about where it has been. Alkaline phosphatase (a bone marker) is up, which oncology follows with the bone disease. Kidney function steady. Cholesterol fine.

documents.title: Missed video visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Reached pt about Tuesday's missed video visit. Her denosumab appointment at the cancer center ran long and she lost track of the time. Offered to rebook; she would rather wait for the fall visit unless something comes up. Message left for PCP.

documents.title: Call from palliative care physician
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Palliative care physician called about yesterday's visit. Ongoing pain and insomnia; Svetlana told them she wants to 'end it all' and asked about physician-assisted death. On direct questions: a wish to die, no plan, no intent, no firearms in the house. Safety plan made with her and her family present. Mirtazapine 7.5 mg at night started for sleep and mood; psycho-oncology referral sent. They asked me to see her this week. Booked Thursday 10/16 at 2 pm. Letter to follow.

documents.title: Palliative care clinic note
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PALLIATIVE CARE - Return visit 10/13/2025

72-year-old woman with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma metastatic to bone, recurrent malignancy-associated hypercalcemia (April and May 2024) and CPPD disease, known to our clinic since August 2024. Accompanied by family.

She has been through more than one line of chemotherapy: capecitabine from June 2024 until progression, and eribulin started last month. Despite her analgesics, pain persists and she sleeps badly. Today she said she wants to just end it all and asked whether we could help her die. She is visibly tired and has lost weight since we last saw her.

Current medications: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, dexamethasone 4 mg daily, acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn, eribulin per oncology, denosumab monthly. Cancer center list also shows letrozole, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Vitals stable. Alert, distressed, tearful at times. Diffuse tenderness over the bones.
Labs: hemoglobin 10.2, calcium 10.5, alkaline phosphatase 240, creatinine 1.1.

Assessment and plan:
1. Suicidal ideation in the setting of advanced cancer, uncontrolled pain and insomnia. Asked directly: a wish to be dead, without a plan or intent; no firearms at home. She agreed to a written safety plan developed with her and her family, including crisis line numbers. Psycho-oncology referral placed. We talked about what she means by help to die and about how much of her suffering we can still treat; she wants to keep talking with us and with her primary care physician.
2. Insomnia and low mood - mirtazapine 7.5 mg at bedtime.
3. Pain - no change to morphine ER or gabapentin today; reassess in two weeks.
4. Calcium 10.5 - oncology aware.
Primary care physician called 10/14.
Return in 2 weeks.

orders.reason: psycho-oncology; passive suicidal ideation with advanced cancer

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen at palliative care's request, three days after she told them she wanted to end it all. Palliative letter arrived this morning and was reviewed before the visit.

S: She came alone, by a friend's car. Says the words came out after a run of nights without sleep and a bad pain week. Wishes the illness would be over and that she could choose when; asked me again about assisted dying. No plan, has not thought about how, no stockpiled pills - her sister holds the morning dose box and the morphine count is checked by palliative care. No firearms. Has not acted on any thought before. Reasons to keep going: her sister and her book club. First mirtazapine nights: slept six hours.
Chemo: capecitabine stopped at the end of the summer, eribulin infusions since September. Pain is in the low back and pelvis, 5/10 today.
PHQ-9 14.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 47.5 kg (down from 50 in April). Thin, tired, tearful once, engaged and future-oriented by the end. Oriented, thought process linear, no psychosis. Diffuse bony tenderness. Heart regular, lungs clear.
Palliative labs 10/13: Hgb 10.2, Ca 10.5, alk phos 240, Cr 1.1.

A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation, passive, without plan or intent, in advanced cancer with pain and insomnia. Safety plan reviewed and a copy scanned; crisis numbers confirmed in her phone. Psychiatry (psycho-oncology) referral placed from here as well so it is tracked. Our nurse will call next week. Discussed that I will keep talking about end-of-life choices with her openly and that wanting control is not something to hide from us.
2. Insomnia/low mood - mirtazapine 7.5 at bedtime from palliative care, added to our list.
3. Metastatic breast cancer - capecitabine off the list, eribulin per oncology.
4. Weight loss - mirtazapine may help appetite; small meals.
Return in 3 months, sooner by message or phone any time.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Check-in call as planned. Pt says she is sleeping better on the new pill, appetite slightly up. Asked directly about thoughts of ending her life: 'the wish is there some days, but I'm not going to do anything.' No plan. Knows the crisis line and our number. Saw palliative care again yesterday. Flu and COVID shots booked for next Tuesday. Will update PCP.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Timed for her off-week from eribulin per oncology. High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccine given. Brief chat: mood 'a little steadier.' No reactions.

documents.title: Psycho-oncology consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Cancer center psycho-oncology service - consultation 11/20/2025.
Referred by palliative care and primary care after expressing a wish to end her life in October.
She describes grief over losing her independence, broken sleep that has improved on mirtazapine, and a persistent wish that things would end, without any plan or intent. No history of self-harm. Supports: sister, a close friend, book club.
Mental status: cooperative, mood 'tired', affect constricted but reactive, linear, no psychotic features, insight good.
Plan: supportive psychotherapy every two weeks here, in person or by video. Continue mirtazapine 7.5 mg at bedtime. Safety plan reviewed and unchanged. We will coordinate with palliative care and primary care.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home. Seeing the psycho-oncology counselor every other week and finds it helps. Sleep 6-7 hours on mirtazapine. Still has days when she wishes it were over; no plan or intent, no change to the safety plan. Eribulin continues; tired the week after each infusion. Pain managed by palliative care.
PHQ-9 11 (14 in October).
Appears tired but engaged, smiling at points.
Plan: continue current care. Office visit with labs in April. Call any time.

documents.title: Oncology progress note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group - visit 2/10/2026, faxed to PCP.
Metastatic breast cancer to bone on eribulin since September 2025, with monthly denosumab. Tolerating treatment with fatigue. Pain managed with palliative care. No hypercalcemia episodes since May 2024.
Plan: continue eribulin and denosumab. Restaging per our schedule. Return in 3 weeks for treatment.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing a bit better in herself. Counseling continues. Sleeping well on mirtazapine. The wish to die comes 'rarely now'; no plan or intent. PHQ-9 8. Eribulin continues with fatigue; pain 3-4 most days. Weight holding.
O: Vitals as charted. Thin, brighter affect than in the fall. Bony tenderness over the low back unchanged. Heart and lungs normal.
A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation - improving; safety plan current, psycho-oncology following.
2. Metastatic breast cancer - oncology/palliative; CMP and CBC today.
3. HTN, lipids - lisinopril and atorvastatin unchanged.
Return late July.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs similar to the fall: calcium normal, hemoglobin mildly low, bone enzyme still raised. Kidney function stable. I've copied oncology.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you renew my blood pressure pill and the cholesterol one? The mail-order company says they need a new prescription.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent lisinopril 20 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg to the mail-order pharmacy, 90 days with refills.

documents.title: Palliative care follow-up
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
Outpatient palliative care - follow-up 6/16/2026 (sent to PCP).
Pain fairly controlled on morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, dexamethasone 4 mg daily and acetaminophen as needed. Sleep improved on mirtazapine 7.5 mg. Mood steadier; continues psycho-oncology. Passive wishes to die are infrequent, no plan or intent; safety plan reviewed. Goals of care discussed with her and her sister: home-focused care, continue eribulin while she tolerates it.
No medication changes. Return in 6 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Steady summer. Eribulin continues every three weeks; fatigue the week after. Pain controlled by palliative care's regimen. Sleep good. Counseling every other week. Passive wishes to die 'hardly ever'; no plan or intent. PHQ-9 7. Home BP 120s-130s.
Meds reviewed, unchanged: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, morphine ER 30 q12h, gabapentin 300 TID, dexamethasone 4, mirtazapine 7.5 qhs, PEG daily, acetaminophen prn; eribulin and denosumab at the cancer center.
O: Vitals as charted; weight stable at 47 kg. Thin. Affect warm. Diffuse low back tenderness unchanged. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation - continues to settle; safety plan in place.
2. Metastatic breast cancer to bone - oncology and palliative care.
3. HTN - controlled on lisinopril.
4. Hyperlipidemia - atorvastatin.
CMP, CBC today. Follow-up booked for September; flu and COVID at that time.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Svetlana, your labs from Friday are much like April's - calcium in range, hemoglobin a little low, kidney function stable. I've sent a copy to oncology. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. See you then.

documents.title: Oncology progress note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group - treatment visit 8/11/2026.
Continues eribulin for metastatic breast cancer to bone, with monthly denosumab. Fatigue stable, counts adequate for treatment. No hypercalcemia. Pain managed with palliative care.
Plan: continue current treatment; next restaging per schedule.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

documents.title: Filed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Oncology note received by fax and filed to Outside Records for PCP review.
